The '''1926 German football championship''', the 19th edition of the competition, was won by [[SpVgg Fürth]], defeating [[Hertha BSC]] 4–1 in the final.<ref name="Rsssf" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duithistpre45.html |title=German championship 1926 |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 8 January 2016}}</ref>

For SpVgg Fürth it was the second national championship after winning the 1914 edition and it won a third and last one in 1929, also against Hertha BSC. For Hertha it marked the club's first final appearance and it played in six consecutive ones, losing the first four and winning the final two in 1930 and 1931.<ref name="List" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html |title=(West) Germany -List of champions |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 8 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/hertha-bsc/1/ |title= Hertha BSC » Steckbrief |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 8 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=Hertha BSC honours}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/spvgg-greuther-fuerth/1/ |title= SpVgg Greuther Fürth » Steckbrief |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 8 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=SpVgg Greuther Fürth honours}}</ref>

Hamburger SV's [[Tull Harder]] was the top scorer of the 1926 championship with six goals, having previously done so in 1922 and 1923 and, again, in 1928.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/deutsche-meisterschaft/ |title=Deutsche Meisterschaft » Torschützenkönige |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 8 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship: Top goal scorer}}</ref>

Sixteen club qualified for the knock-out competition, two from each of the regional federations plus an additional third club from the South and West. In all cases the regional champions and runners-up qualified. In the West and South the third spot went to the third placed team of the championship.<ref name="Rsssf" />

The eventual champions, SpVgg Fürth, failed to qualify for the Southern German championship through the [[Bezirksliga Bayern]], coming only third behind league champions [[FC Bayern Munich]] runners-up [[1. FC Nürnberg]], when only the champions advanced. Instead, Fürth won the Southern German Cup and qualified through this route for the Southern German finals where it than finished runners-up.<ref>Hyll, page 82</ref>
